title: Plan AL: AI Social Content Calendar
summary: Audience profile → topic pool → scheduling → batch creation → attribution
scenario: For teams planning monthly multi-platform social content — turning scattered creation into a steady calendar.

steps.title: Audience profile
steps.detail: Combine account analytics and competitor research to extract the audience's pains, topics and content preferences. Have the model produce a 'reader persona card' to guide every topic choice.
steps.tips: Make the persona concrete down to 'which keywords they search' — topics and copy then write themselves.

steps.title: Topic pool
steps.detail: Generate 20-30 topics from the persona, classified as informational / emotional / promotional and scored. Leave room for trend slots and breaking news.
steps.tips: Keep the monthly pool at 30 topics, over-deliver, top it up as it drains.

steps.title: Scheduling
steps.detail: Build a content calendar in Notion's calendar view, assigning topics to dates and platforms with owners and status. Set three-stage reminders: draft due, review, publish.
steps.tips: Fix weekdays as update days and weekends for long-form or engagement posts — an expected rhythm.

steps.title: Batch creation
steps.detail: Dedicate half a day weekly to batch-generating copy and images per the calendar, using fixed templates for a consistent look. Stage drafts in a Notion 'to publish' board, queue after review.
steps.tips: Lock the structure and tone for the batch so the week reads like one voice.

steps.title: Attribution
steps.detail: Use automation to pool platform metrics in one place; at month's end, have the model compare topic type, timing and engagement. Write 'what works' into next month's plan.
steps.tips: Attribute by topic type rather than single posts — aggregated conclusions are steadier.

pitfalls.title: Scheduled but never executed
pitfalls.detail: A pretty calendar that nobody acts on is zero; assign an owner and due date to every item.

pitfalls.title: Homogenized batch content
pitfalls.detail: Over-templating creates an assembly-line feel; keep ~20% hand-crafted.

pitfalls.title: Ignoring data
pitfalls.detail: Publishing without reviewing feedback is broadcasting into the void; review monthly.

pitfalls.title: No room for trends
pitfalls.detail: A full calendar has no slack; leave 2-3 slots weekly for what's hot.
